bug_semantics: The Renovate gleam manager (lib/modules/manager/gleam/artifacts.ts) built the lockfile-update command by string-joining attacker-controlled dependency names into a single shell command: `['gleam deps update', ...packagesToUpdate].join(' ')` passed to exec, which runs through a shell. A repository maintainer can craft a gleam.toml whose dependency name contains shell metacharacters (e.g. `$(...)`), so when Renovate runs `gleam deps update <depName>` the shell evaluates the injected text before gleam parses it, executing arbitrary commands on the Renovate runtime (CWE-78 OS Command Injection).
flaw_origin: Commit d29698e0131231652970f02765312769975e4d38 ("feat(manager/gleam): enable update-lockfile (#31002)", 2024-12-06, author Jason Sipula <SnakeDoc@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub, no AI trailers) replaced the fixed `gleam deps download` command with `const packagesToUpdate = ... updatedDeps.map((dep) => dep.depName).filter(Boolean); const updateCommand = ['gleam deps update', ...packagesToUpdate].join(' '); await exec(updateCommand, execOptions)` — depName values come from the repository's gleam.toml and are interpolated into a shell command without quoting or sanitization. The advisory's named sink (depName appended to gleam deps update commands without sanitization) is created by this commit; parent 9c999fb13e ran only the constant command. The manager itself (283cda0f29d1, #30345, 2024-07-31) created artifacts.ts but executed only the constant `gleam deps download`.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object names author Jason Sipula, committer GitHub, plain human message (#31002) with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or bot/AI identity (grep NONE sentinel).
evidence: Advisory (CVE-2026-76233 / GHSA-xmpw-q5r4-p783): Renovate from 39.53.0 before 40.33.0 — command injection in the gleam manager where the depName parameter is appended to gleam deps update commands without proper sanitization; attackers with repository write access craft malicious gleam.toml files to execute arbitrary commands on the machine running Renovate.

BIC creation check: d29698e01312 (#31002, 2024-12-06) changes gleam/artifacts.ts from `await exec('gleam deps download', execOptions)` to building `const updateCommand = ['gleam deps update', ...packagesToUpdate].join(' ')` where `packagesToUpdate = updatedDeps.map((dep) => dep.depName).filter(Boolean)` — depName originates from the repository's gleam.toml, joined unquoted into a shell-executed string. Parent 9c999fb13e8 has only the constant command.

Fix commit 59de985bb27c (#36163, 2025-05-27, Anne Stellingwerf, "fix(managers): quote more manager commands"): adds `import { quote } from 'shlex'` and changes to `...packagesToUpdate.map(quote)` in gleam/artifacts.ts (plus 10 other manager files) — quoting the attacker-controlled depName proves the unquoted join is the defect.

Version boundary: BIC d29698e01312 is an ancestor of tag 39.53.0 (first tag containing it is 39.53.0, matching the advisory's introduced version); fix 59de985bb27c is an ancestor of tag 40.33.0, matching the advisory's fixed version.

AI-marker screening: `git log --format='%an <%ae>%n%cn <%ce>%n%B' -1` on d29698e01312, 283cda0f29d1, 59de985bb27c — human authors only (283cda0f29d1 has human Co-authored-by: cdaringe/Rhys Arkins/Michael Kriese trailers, which are not AI markers); grep for claude/copilot/anthropic/openai/generated/cursor/junie finds nothing (NONE sentinels).

ppa re-checked line-level 2026-08-29 against clone history: git show 9c999fb1:lib/modules/manager/gleam/artifacts.ts executes the literal 'gleam deps download' with no package list; the vulnerable ['gleam deps update', ...packagesToUpdate].join(' ') passed to exec is introduced by the BIC d29698e0 diff. -> introducer_parent_absent=true.
reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory names depName appended to gleam deps update commands without sanitization; the BIC diff shows exactly the unquoted `['gleam deps update', ...packagesToUpdate].join(' ')` fed to shell-executing exec(), and the fix applies shlex quote to the same array — proving the unsanitized interpolation is the defect. BIC choice: d29698e01312 created the named sink — before it the manager ran only a constant command, so no attacker-controlled data reached a shell; the advisory's introduced-version 39.53.0 matches the first tag containing this commit.
